clue.text: Boy and girl in South Asian region

parts.note: Ben is a common boy's name
gal is an informal word for a girl

explanation.surface: Two young people turn up somewhere on the Indian subcontinent.
explanation.definitionFit: Bengal is the historic region now split between eastern India and Bangladesh.

clue.text: Boat carrying nothing extravagant

indicators.note: carrying says the boat holds the nothing inside

parts.note: a barque is a sailing ship
nothing is zero, the letter O

explanation.surface: An empty boat that is nonetheless lavish.
explanation.definitionFit: Baroque describes the ornate, highly decorated style of 17th-century art, hence over-elaborate.

clue.text: Storytelling has arrived in the country

indicators.note: in says the arrived abbreviation goes inside the country

parts.note: a nation is a country
arr is the timetable abbreviation for arrived

explanation.surface: Storytelling has come to the land.
explanation.definitionFit: Narration is the act of telling a story or giving an account.

clue.text: Excited, getting a line in musical

indicators.note: in says the line letter goes inside the musical

parts.note: Fame is a stage musical, from the 1980 film

explanation.surface: Someone thrilled to get a part in a stage show.
explanation.definitionFit: Aflame literally means on fire, and figuratively burning with passion or eagerness.

clue.text: One sweeping around everyone in dance hall

indicators.note: around says the sweeper's word is wrapped about the word for everyone

parts.note: a broom is the thing that does the sweeping
everyone means all

explanation.surface: A cleaner sweeps round everybody in a dance venue.
explanation.definitionFit: A ballroom is a large room built for formal dancing, a hall for dances.

clue.text: Top copy on end of fax

indicators.note: on says the copy word sits above the next piece in this down answer

parts.note: to ape is to copy or mimic

indicators.note: end of takes the final letter of fax

explanation.surface: A duplicate sitting on the last page of a fax.
explanation.definitionFit: The apex is the highest point or peak of something.

clue.text: Newspaper entering shabby motels, sinister in the extreme

indicators.note: entering says the newspaper goes inside the jumbled letters
shabby says the word motels is knocked out of shape

parts.note: FT is the Financial Times newspaper

explanation.surface: A paper delivered to run-down motels in a creepy extreme.
explanation.walkthrough: 'shabby' rearranges MOTELS to LEMOST, which FT is 'entering'. Sinister means left in Latin and heraldry, so it is not menacing here.
explanation.definitionFit: Sinister means left, and leftmost is as far left as possible, its extreme.

clue.text: Dramatic performance by leader of extremists during chat show, cut

indicators.note: during says that letter goes in the middle of the trimmed show
cut says the show's name is shortened, losing a letter

parts.note: Oprah was Oprah Winfrey's long-running chat show

indicators.note: leader of takes the first letter of extremists

explanation.surface: A dramatic act by the head of a radical group on a talk show gets edited out.
explanation.definitionFit: An opera is a staged drama set to music, a theatrical performance.

clue.text: Brownish-yellow feature in something brown

indicators.note: in says the feature word goes inside something brown

parts.note: mud is something brown
to star is to feature, as an actor in a film

explanation.surface: A yellowish tinge appears in a brown object.
explanation.definitionFit: Mustard names a dull yellow colour, after the condiment.

clue.text: A bank adhering to minimum of regulations, not so often

indicators.note: adhering to says the following pieces stick on beside the opening letter
the minimum of a word is its smallest part, its opening letter

parts.note: to bank on someone is to rely on them

explanation.surface: A lender that only just keeps to the rules, and seldom at that.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bank' looks like a lender but is the verb, as in bank on.
explanation.definitionFit: Rarely means seldom, on few occasions; 'not so often' is a looser way of saying infrequently.

clue.text: Character lying back in meadows, bare in winter?

indicators.note: in says the turned word sits inside the meadows word

parts.note: a lea is a meadow, a poetic word

indicators.note: lying back says the word for character is read in the opposite direction

parts.note: one's character is one's self

explanation.surface: Someone reclining in fields notices trees stripped for winter.
explanation.definitionFit: Deciduous trees shed their foliage, so in winter they stand bare, without any leaves; the question mark flags it as a description by example.

clue.text: Work unit holding European up as potential killer

indicators.note: in a down answer up means the whole is read from the bottom
holding says the work unit is wrapped round the European

parts.note: the erg is a unit of work in physics
a Dane, from Denmark, is a European

explanation.surface: A workplace team holding a European citizen captive, seen as a danger.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up' reverses the whole assembly, so the European must be read backwards inside the work unit as well.
explanation.definitionFit: A grenade is a small bomb that could kill if it goes off.

clue.text: Entanglement, meeting between the sheets

indicators.note: between says the meeting goes in among the sheets

parts.note: a quire is a set of 24 or 25 sheets of paper
AGM is an annual general meeting

explanation.surface: A tangled affair, a rendezvous in bed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'between the sheets' suggests bed, but the sheets are paper, a quire.
explanation.definitionFit: A quagmire is a bog, and figuratively a messy predicament one is caught up in.

clue.text: Monkey according to an antelope

parts.note: a monkey is a mischievous child, an imp
a la (from French) means in the manner of, according to

explanation.surface: A primate claims something is an antelope.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Monkey' is the cheeky child, not the animal.
explanation.definitionFit: The impala is a graceful African antelope known for its leaping.

clue.text: Cat in China is reportedly doing a backflip

indicators.note: doing a backflip says the hidden letters are read backwards
the clue word that says the letters sit inside the next words

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A cat in China is said to be doing acrobatics.
explanation.walkthrough: No word says 'hidden': the letters sit across the words China is reportedly, and 'doing a backflip' turns them round in this down answer.
explanation.definitionFit: The Persian is a long-haired breed of domestic cat.

clue.text: Way out is no longer the thing

parts.note: ex means former, no longer so
it means the very thing, as in 'that's it'

explanation.surface: The way out has stopped being fashionable.
explanation.definitionFit: An exit is a door or passage for leaving a place.

clue.text: Minute to clear zone in sudden riot, not half disorganised

indicators.note: in says the cleared zone goes inside the jumble
disorganised says the letters are thrown out of order
not half means only the first half of the word riot is kept
to clear the word zone is to empty its middle, keeping its ends

explanation.surface: Riot police move in to clear an area during a sudden disturbance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to clear' empties ZONE to ZE, and 'not half' cuts riot to RI; 'disorganised' jumbles SUDDEN RI, and ZE goes 'in' it.
explanation.definitionFit: Minute (my-NEWT) means tiny, and something undersized is smaller than normal.

clue.text: Wine that's unknown in cooler having shown up

parts.note: Z is an algebraic unknown
a fan is something that cools

indicators.note: in a down answer up means the word is read from the bottom

parts.note: having shown the way is having led

explanation.surface: Wine that has turned up unannounced in the cool box.
explanation.definitionFit: Zinfandel is a red grape variety grown chiefly in California, and the wine made from it.

clue.text: Somewhat devious, easy parts

indicators.note: parts means splits open, so the devious word is split to take the easy word

parts.note: sly means devious or cunning
light means easy, as in light work

explanation.surface: A rather crafty, undemanding role in a play.
explanation.walkthrough: 'parts' looks like a noun (acting roles) but is the verb splits.
explanation.definitionFit: Slightly means to a small degree, a little, much like somewhat.

clue.text: Boycott clearing sightscreen helps openers for cricketing nation

parts.note: to boycott is to ban
a glade is a clearing in a wood

indicators.note: openers are the opening letters of the words sightscreen and helps

explanation.surface: Geoffrey Boycott, the England opening batsman, clears the sightscreen and the openers benefit.
explanation.walkthrough: Geoffrey Boycott was a famous England opening batsman; a sightscreen is the white screen behind the bowler that helps batsmen see the ball.
explanation.definitionFit: Bangladesh plays Test cricket, so it is a nation known for the sport.

clue.text: Forecast wind in wine shops

parts.note: to bode is to portend or forecast
wind means gas in the stomach

explanation.surface: Predicting flatulence among the wine merchants.
explanation.definitionFit: A bodega is a Spanish wine shop or cellar, and bodegas is its plural.

clue.text: Animals warbled, travelling west

indicators.note: in an across answer travelling west means read from right to left

parts.note: to warble is to sing, so warbled means sung

explanation.surface: Creatures sing as they migrate westward.
explanation.definitionFit: Gnus, also called wildebeest, are large African antelopes, so they are animals by example.

clue.text: Vague, pompous commercial breaks

indicators.note: breaks says the commercial interrupts the pompous word

parts.note: showy means ostentatious, pompous
an ad is a commercial, an advertisement

explanation.surface: Pretentious adverts interrupting a programme, but nothing clear.
explanation.walkthrough: 'commercial breaks' reads as a TV phrase, but 'breaks' is the verb putting AD inside.
explanation.definitionFit: Shadowy means dim and indistinct, hard to make out, so vague.

clue.text: Preserve confidence

definitions.meaning: to preserve fruit is to ... it in jars
in British slang, nerve or courage

explanation.surface: Keep your nerve.
explanation.definitionFit: To bottle is to preserve food in jars, and in British slang bottle means nerve or courage.

clue.text: Doctor on leave, Aussie twit

parts.note: to leave is to go

explanation.surface: A medic on holiday is a fool, Australians say.
explanation.definitionFit: Drongo is Australian slang for a stupid or useless person, named after a bird.

clue.text: Asian lady wiping brow with bottom of sari

indicators.note: wiping the brow removes the top letter of the word for lady in this down answer

parts.note: a lady is a woman

indicators.note: bottom of takes the last letter of sari, at the foot of the word

explanation.surface: A woman in a sari mops her forehead with its hem.
explanation.definitionFit: An Omani is a person from Oman, a country on the Arabian Peninsula in western Asia.

clue.text: View otherwise obscured by hat

indicators.note: obscured by says the word for otherwise is covered up inside the hat

parts.note: a panama is a lightweight straw hat
or means otherwise, as in 'hurry or you will miss it'

explanation.surface: A view that would be fine except a hat blocks it.
explanation.definitionFit: A panorama is a wide, unbroken view of a landscape.

clue.text: Emperor in pants, a rapscallion

indicators.note: in says the letters lie inside the words pants, a rapscallion

explanation.surface: A ruler caught in his underwear, a rogue.
explanation.definitionFit: A tsar was the emperor of Russia before 1917.

clue.text: Amazon in South America initially gets redirected

indicators.note: redirected says these letters are sent in a new order
initially takes the first letters of the words South and America

explanation.surface: Someone in South America gets sent another way, perhaps along the Amazon river.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests the river; Amazon here is a tall, strong woman.
explanation.definitionFit: An Amazon, after the mythical female warriors, is a tall powerful woman, which a giantess is.

clue.text: Moon behind the boss in the workplace

indicators.note: behind says the moon comes after the boss

parts.note: a boss is a knob or stud on a surface
Io is a moon of Jupiter

explanation.surface: Someone mooning behind the boss at the office.
explanation.walkthrough: 'the boss' is not a manager but a raised ornament, a stud.
explanation.definitionFit: A studio is a room where an artist, photographer or broadcaster works.

clue.text: Odd bits broken off simply held in fragment, where vessels built

indicators.note: held in says those letters sit inside the fragment

parts.note: a shard is a broken fragment, of glass or pottery

indicators.note: breaking off the odd bits of simply leaves its second, fourth and sixth letters

explanation.surface: Pieces snapped off are stuck back into a broken piece at a shipbuilding works.
explanation.definitionFit: A shipyard is the place where ships are constructed and repaired.

clue.text: Very unstable ultimately during partial recovery

indicators.note: during says that letter falls in the middle of the recovery

parts.note: a rally is a partial recovery, of prices or health

indicators.note: ultimately points to the final letter of unstable

explanation.surface: Markets stay shaky even as prices partly bounce back.
explanation.definitionFit: Really is an intensifier meaning extremely, as in 'really good'.
